inputs.original_text: Calling Senate Bill 175 a “limited safeguard” doesn’t make it harmless. Restricting new registrants in state elections still puts another barrier between people and the ballot, while “confidence” rhetoric can make exclusion sound like responsible governance. Voting should be accessible, and any state rule that narrows who gets to participate deserves serious scrutiny—not a presumption that it protects democracy.
inputs.modified_text: Senate Bill 175 is being sold as a modest safeguard, but limiting new registrants’ access to state elections is still a decision to make participation harder. Appeals to “confidence” can disguise exclusion as good governance, shifting the burden onto voters rather than fixing institutions. The right to vote should be accessible; any rule that narrows participation deserves scrutiny, not automatic trust.
